prior_questions: Does the second reprint define a covered data center and support the asserted 100 MW threshold and specific scope?
records.resolution: Official second reprint supplies the missing final definition, strict demand threshold, aggregation and tariff safeguards. Retained final pocket-veto history is hash-verified. Scope inclusion is limited to the versioned infrastructure-policy observation; no enactment or facility-specific eligibility is claimed.

field_changes.before: The second reprint would have required utility tariff protections for other customers against costs from commercial large-load customers at centralized facilities with aggregate monthly demand exceeding 100 MW; facilities could be aggregated based on ownership, control and infrastructure. Qualifying data centers could be covered, but the final definition was not data-center-specific.
field_changes.after: Pocket-vetoed second reprint proposed utility tariffs for centralized commercial facilities with aggregate monthly demand over 100 MW, aggregable by ownership, control and infrastructure. Its final definition replaced the earlier data-center-specific language. Proposed safeguards included cost allocation, stranded-cost protection, financial guarantees covering at least 85% of requested service for at least 10 years, and security deposits, with BPU relaxation for sufficient operational flexibility or added energy/capacity. These failed-bill terms are not current tariff requirements.
